analysis.title: Magna International Inc. (MGA): 2026 EPS guidance unchanged; Ability to offset difficult market/industry dynamics with company specific efforts in focus; 3Q26 wrap
key_insights: GS reiterates Sell on Magna (MGA). 12m price target raised to $56 from $55 (MG.TO C$78 from C$77), implying 12.3% downside from $63.82. Target is 7x normalized EPS of $8.05 (from $7.90 prior).
3Q26 adjusted EBIT of $683 mn beat the Street ($623 mn) and GS ($611 mn). Adjusted EBIT margin was 6.8% vs GS 6.0% and Street 6.2%. Adjusted EPS was $1.83 vs Street $1.58 and GS $1.51.

3Q26 revenue was $10.1 bn, down 8% qoq, down 4% yoy and down 2% organically, in line with Street $10.1 bn and GS $10.2 bn. Growth over market was 0.5% on weighted markets, about 1% excluding Complete Vehicles.

CY26 guidance midpoints were lowered for revenue and adjusted EBIT margin, citing lower China production and program mix. Revenue is now $41.2-42.0 bn (midpoint $41.6 bn) from $41.3-42.5 bn. EBIT margin is 6.3-6.5% from 6.3-6.6%.
CY26 adjusted EPS guidance midpoint is unchanged at $7.00 (range $6.85-7.15 vs $6.70-7.30 prior), helped by lower net interest expense and a lower tax rate. Street is $7.05 and GS prior was $7.00.

Implied 4Q26 guidance midpoint is well below prior GS and Street numbers: revenue $10.2 bn, adjusted EBIT $745 mn, margin 7.3%, EPS $1.93. GS prior was $10.6 bn / $867 mn / 8.2% / $2.27 and Street $10.5 bn / $832 mn / 7.9% / $2.23.

CY26 FCF outlook raised to $1.85-1.90 bn from $1.75-1.85 bn. Capex is about $1.5 bn (from $1.5-1.6 bn). In 3Q Magna generated about $584 mn adjusted FCF, paid $129 mn in dividends and repurchased $529 mn of shares.
Magna completed its existing buyback in October (remaining 1.3 mn shares) and its board approved a new NCIB for 25.8 mn shares.

Input costs worsened in 3Q and 4Q versus the prior outlook, with a 50 bp headwind in 3Q and a similar headwind expected in 4Q. Steel and aluminum are covered by resale or pass-through. About 40% of resins is index-protected. DRAM and electronic components show the largest increases and recoveries must largely be negotiated with customers.
Operational excellence is tracking toward 50 bp of margin improvement in 2026 vs an initial 35-40 bp, with another 35-40 bp targeted for 2027.
Magna is upfitting vehicles for Waymo in Arizona and now works on two new vehicle models. Divestitures of low-margin businesses (e.g. Lighting and Rooftop Systems) are largely complete.

GS Sell thesis rests on Magna's historically below-average growth over market, EMEA exposure (tariffs and competition), and incremental input cost pressure shared with other tier 1 suppliers. GS will assess longer-term growth and margin potential at the November investor day.
GS estimate changes: CY26/27/28 EPS to $7.05/$7.65/$8.25 from $7.00/$7.60/$8.20 on lower share count, lower interest expense and lower revenue. CY26 revenue estimate is $41,653 mn (from $42,140 mn).

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Sell and raises target to $56 from $55 on 7x normalized EPS of $8.05. It cites below-average growth over market, EMEA exposure and input cost pressure, with 12.3% downside to the target.

sector_views.rationale: Tier 1 suppliers face incremental input cost pressure, especially DRAM and electronic components, with recoveries needing customer negotiation. A sluggish production backdrop makes growth over market more important.

earnings_insights: Magna 3Q26 reported (10/30): adjusted EPS $1.83 vs Street consensus $1.58 and GS estimate $1.51. Non-GAAP EBIT $683 mn vs Street $623 mn and GS $611 mn. Revenue $10.1 bn vs Street $10.1 bn and GS $10.2 bn.

3Q26 segment adjusted EBIT: Body Exteriors & Structures $387 mn (9.3% margin), Power & Vision $287 mn (7.6%), Seating Systems $28 mn (2.2%), Complete Vehicles $33 mn (3.3%), Corporate & Other -$52 mn.

CY26 guidance: revenue $41.2-42.0 bn (midpoint $41.6 bn, vs Street $41.9 bn and GS prior $42.1 bn), adjusted EBIT margin 6.3-6.5%, adjusted EPS $6.85-7.15 (midpoint $7.00 vs Street $7.05), FCF $1.85-1.90 bn.
Implied 4Q26 guidance at midpoint: revenue $10.18 bn, adjusted EBIT $745 mn (14.1% below GS prior, 10.5% below Street), adjusted EPS $1.93 vs GS prior $2.27 and Street $2.23.
GS forecasts (estimates): CY26E EPS $7.05, CY27E $7.65, CY28E $8.25. Next quarters: 4Q26E EPS $2.01 (as printed in the key data table), 1Q27E $1.29, 2Q27E $1.99.
Company CY26 light vehicle production assumptions: North America 15.0 mn (unchanged), China 30.4 mn (from 31.2 mn), Europe 16.8 mn (unchanged).

trade_ideas.description: Sell rating on MGA with 12-month price target of $56 (MG.TO C$78), 12.3% downside from $63.82
trade_ideas.rationale: Below-average historical growth over market, EMEA exposure and incremental input cost pressures outweigh operational improvements and divestitures.
trade_ideas.risk: Share gains and growth with key customers, content per vehicle growth, faster EBIT margin and FCF improvement, a better auto cycle or more favorable tariff rules.

risk_factors: Upside risks to the Sell: Magna gains share (key customers, Asia presence).
Upside risks: Magna grows content per vehicle and outgrows industry production, including pivoting to secular growth areas sooner than GS expects.
Upside risks: EBIT margins and FCF improve faster than GS estimates.
Upside risks: a better auto cycle or more favorable tariff rules.
Input cost inflation, especially DRAM and electronics, with recoveries dependent on customer negotiations.
Lower China light vehicle production and unfavorable program mix.
geopolitical: The report cites tariffs and competition as making growth harder in EMEA, and notes tariff rules as an upside or downside swing factor.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong operational execution (about 90 bp yoy operating margin increase in 3Q, partly timing of recoveries), 50 bp of 2026 operational efficiency gains with more in 2027, higher FCF outlook, continued buybacks and divestiture of low-margin businesses should help growth and margins over time.
tension_points.bear_case: Magna has historically grown below market, EMEA faces tariff and competition pressure, input costs (DRAM, electronics, resins) are worsening, and 4Q implied guidance sits well below GS and Street estimates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Magna gaining share, outgrowing industry production through content per vehicle, or improving EBIT margins and FCF faster than GS estimates, or a better auto cycle or more favorable tariffs.
